title: अकबर के दरबार में बीरबल का प्रवेश
summary: एक चतुर युवक महेश दास ने अपनी हाज़िरजवाबी और न्यायप्रियता से सम्राट अकबर का दिल जीतकर दरबारी बीरबल बनने का गौरव प्राप्त किया।

title: राज्य में कितने कौवे हैं?
summary: सम्राट अकबर ने दरबारियों से पूछा कि आगरा में कुल कितने कौवे हैं; बीरबल के चतुराई भरे उत्तर ने सबको निरुत्तर कर दिया।

title: How Many Crows?
summary: A skeptical visiting nobleman challenges Birbal to verify his famous bird count. Birbal teaches him that truth requires evidence, not mere contradiction.

title: बीरबल की खिचड़ी
summary: ठिठुरती ठंड में यमुना के पानी में रात बिताने वाले ग़रीब धोबी को न्याय दिलाने के लिए बीरबल ने पकाई अनोखी खिचड़ी।

title: The Brahmin's Dream
summary: A greedy moneylender demands real gold from a poor scholar who borrowed money in a dream. Birbal settles the debt with a looking glass.

title: The Question of Heirs
summary: Three estranged brothers claim their late father's hidden treasure. Birbal uses an emotional test to reveal the genuine son.

title: Birbal Identifies the Thief
summary: When a merchant's diamond ring is stolen by one of his trusted servants, Birbal distributes magic bamboo sticks that magically solve the mystery.

title: The Lost Ring
summary: Akbar loses his favorite emerald ring inside the royal council chamber. Birbal identifies the thief among the imperial courtiers with a clever whisper.

title: The Farmer's Dispute
summary: A cunning landlord sells a well to a poor farmer, then demands rent for the water inside. Birbal turns the contract against the trickster.

title: Akbar and the Line Drawing
summary: Akbar challenges his courtiers to make a chalk line shorter without touching or erasing it. Birbal reveals a profound lesson in nobility.

title: Birbal and the Jealous Courtiers
summary: Jealous ministers plot with the royal barber to send Birbal to heaven on a suicide mission. Birbal's foresight turns the deadly trap upon the conspirators.

title: The Gold Coins and the Judge
summary: A dishonest Qazi steals gold coins entrusted to him by a traveling pilgrim. Birbal uses fresh wax and olive oil to expose the judicial crime.

title: The Boy Who Wanted to Meet Akbar
summary: A poor village boy uses clever answers to bypass palace guards and win an audience with the Great Mughal Emperor.

title: Birbal and the Painter
summary: A miserly merchant refuses to pay a portrait painter by constantly altering his facial expressions. Birbal provides the painter with a flawless remedy.

title: The Three Baskets
summary: Akbar orders Birbal to fill three baskets with Truth, Illusion, and Falsehood. Birbal returns with three everyday objects that embody profound philosophy.

title: Birbal's Khichdi
summary: When Akbar refuses to reward a poor washerman who survived a freezing night in the river, Birbal cooks khichdi over a distant fire to awaken the Emperor's conscience.

title: The Biggest Thing?
summary: Akbar asks his court to name the largest entity in the universe. Birbal answers with a truth that touches the Emperor's soul.

title: The Wilted Flower
summary: A fawning courtier claims his garden flowers never fade under Akbar's glorious reign. Birbal uses a simple bee to prick the bubble of sycophancy.

title: The Four Fools
summary: Akbar orders Birbal to bring the four greatest fools of Agra to court. Birbal presents two absurd strangers and names the remaining two with brilliant audacity.

title: The Mango Thief
summary: Two men claim ownership of a sweet mango tree laden with ripe fruit. Birbal uses a Solomon-like test to determine the authentic planter.

title: The Cost of a Dream
summary: A miserly merchant demands real money from a neighbor who dreamed of borrowing gold. Birbal ensures the settlement matches the reality of the claim.

title: The Stolen Pearl
summary: A priceless pearl vanishes from Akbar's private chamber. Birbal uncovers which attendant took it by observing their nervous eyes.

title: Birbal's Wisdom vs Tansen's Music
summary: Akbar asks whether Tansen's heavenly music or Birbal's sharp wit is more essential to the empire. Birbal orchestrates a gentle demonstration.

title: The Price of Buttermilk
summary: A dishonest milkman waters down his milk to double his profits. A clever monkey ensures poetic justice by dividing the ill-gotten gains.

title: The Two Men and the Tree
summary: A dishonest traveler denies receiving a loan under an old banyan tree. Birbal summons the tree as a witness, causing the crook to confess.

title: The Pot of Buttermilk
summary: Akbar orders every citizen to pour one cup of pure milk into a royal pool under cover of darkness. In the morning, the reservoir reveals human nature.

title: The Farmer's Well and Neighbour
summary: A stubborn landlord sells his deep brick well, then forbids the buyer from drawing water without separate payment. Birbal's verdict turns the law upon the deceiver.

title: The King and the Barber
summary: A vain royal barber dreams of royal power and schemes to replace Birbal with himself. Birbal assigns the barber a royal task that quickly cures his delusions.

title: Birbal and the Washerman
summary: Akbar accidentally encounters a washerman upon waking and experiences bad luck, sentencing the innocent man to death. Birbal shows the Emperor whose face was truly unlucky.

title: The Rich Merchant and His Sons
summary: A dying merchant asks Akbar to choose which of his three sons should inherit his estate. Birbal gives each son one copper coin to fill a room.

title: The Honest Woodcutter and Akbar
summary: Akbar meets an old woodcutter singing joyfully despite poverty. Birbal shows the Emperor why peace of mind cannot be bought with an imperial treasury.

title: The Half Reward
summary: A greedy gatekeeper demands half the reward of a poor poet presenting verses to the Emperor. Birbal ensures the guard receives exactly what he asked for.

title: The King and the Beggar's Son
summary: Akbar boasts that every human being bows before his imperial majesty. Birbal introduces a little beggar boy who refuses to bow to pride.

title: The Language of Birds
summary: Akbar asks Birbal to interpret the screeching of two owls on a ruined wall. Birbal delivers a powerful political parable on governance and taxation.

title: The Smell of Food and Sound of Coin
summary: A greedy sweetmaker demands payment from a penniless beggar who inhaled the aroma of frying jalebis. Birbal pays the baker with the clinking sound of silver.

title: The Stingy Seth
summary: A miserly merchant buries his gold coins under a tree and weeps when a thief replaces them with a stone. Birbal reveals that unused wealth has no value.

title: Birbal and the Persian Scholar
summary: An arrogant linguist challenges Akbar's court to discover his true mother tongue. Birbal solves the puzzle in the middle of the night.

title: The Challenge of the Invisible Thread
summary: A foreign weaver claims to have woven a garment of invisible silk that only the truly wise can see. Birbal outsmarts the fraud with his own invisible reward.

title: The Donkey and the Horse
summary: A courtier mocks a poor farmer's donkey, claiming the Emperor's warhorse belongs to a superior universe. Birbal arranges a race of endurance.

title: The Most Important Person
summary: Akbar asks his court who is the most powerful person in the empire. Courtiers name the Emperor, but Birbal points to an unexpected ruler.

title: Birbal and the Witch
summary: Hysteria grips Agra over rumors of a witch haunting the cemetery. Birbal investigates the supernatural terror and unmasks a band of thieves.

title: The Two Friends
summary: Two childhood companions test their bond when one becomes a wealthy minister and the other remains a poor scholar. Birbal illustrates the sacred law of loyalty.

title: The Lost Camel
summary: Birbal describes a missing camel in flawless detail despite never having seen it, demonstrating the power of pure observation.

title: The Talking Parrot
summary: Akbar decrees that whoever brings news of his favorite parrot's death shall be executed. When the bird dies, Birbal delivers the news without speaking the fatal words.

title: Birbal and the Gardener
summary: A poor palace gardener accidentally breaks Akbar's favorite china vase. Birbal helps the honest man turn an imperial death sentence into forgiveness.

title: The Price of Pride
summary: A boastful wrestler claims he can lift anything in the empire. Birbal challenges him to lift a single grain of sand under impossible conditions.

title: Birbal and the Astrologer
summary: A fraudulent astrologer predicts that Akbar will die if he leaves the palace on a Tuesday. Birbal reveals the astrologer's ignorance with an unexpected question.

title: The Weight of an Elephant
summary: Akbar is challenged to weigh a massive war elephant without a scale. Birbal uses water displacement and riverboats to solve the riddle.

title: The Man Who Wanted to be God
summary: An arrogant ascetic claims he has attained divine godhood and demands worship. Birbal tests his claim with a task only God can perform.

title: Birbal and the Village Headman
summary: A corrupt village headman robs poor peasants while claiming full loyalty to the crown. Birbal uses a feast of wild thorns to expose the tyrant.

title: Birbal and the Thief's Beard
summary: When a courtier's gold purse disappears during a crowded festival, Birbal uncovers the thief by making a casual remark about beards.

title: The Thief's Beard Grows - Most famous
summary: Birbal uses the famous folk belief of growing beards to trap an elusive burglar who robbed the imperial jewelers.

title: The Stolen Horse
summary: Two men claim ownership of a magnificent Arabian horse. Birbal asks the horse itself to reveal its real master.

title: The Ghost in the Palace
summary: Terrifying groans and floating lights in the old palace wing terrify guards. Birbal spends the night and catches the 'ghost.'

title: The Most Beautiful Child
summary: Akbar boasts of his handsome princes and challenges Birbal to find the most beautiful child in Agra. Birbal brings an astonishing answer.

title: The Pot of Gold
summary: A peasant finds buried gold on land he just bought and insists on returning it to the seller. Birbal resolves the noble dispute.

title: The Talking Cave
summary: Birbal retells an ancient fable to Akbar to explain why intelligence must always verify situations before taking action.

title: The Foolish Servant
summary: A nobleman boasts of his servant's absolute, unquestioning obedience. Birbal proves that mindless obedience without common sense is dangerous.

title: The Old Woman's Blessing
summary: Akbar rescues an old woman's cow from a ditch and receives a blessing that puzzles his courtiers. Birbal explains the beauty of the old woman's words.

title: The Stone That Speaks
summary: A quarrelsome merchant challenges Birbal to make an ordinary street stone speak in court. Birbal demonstrates that silence itself can speak volumes.

title: The Cost of Sleep
summary: Akbar complains of insomnia on a bed of royal velvet, while an exhausted sentry sleeps soundly on cold stone. Birbal reveals the secret of sweet sleep.

title: Birbal and the Three Questions
summary: A foreign philosopher challenges Akbar's court with three impossible metaphysical questions. Birbal answers all three with brilliant simplicity.

title: The Farmer and the King
summary: A poor farmer offers Akbar a basket of wild plums, while a wealthy prince offers jewels. Birbal reveals which gift was truly greater.

title: The King and the Onion
summary: A merchant claims onions are a rare delicacy and sells them to Akbar for gold. Birbal ensures the merchant receives poetic repayment with garlic.

title: Birbal and the Donkey
summary: Jealous courtiers try to insult Birbal by comparing him to a donkey. Birbal turns the joke upon them with effortless wit.

title: The Language of Animals
summary: Akbar wishes he could understand what animals say. Birbal shows him that understanding human suffering is far more urgent.

title: The Four Questions
summary: Akbar tests Birbal with four philosophical questions on life, death, fear, and joy. Birbal delivers four profound answers.

title: The Blind Men
summary: Birbal retells the ancient parable of the blind men and the elephant to settle a bitter religious dispute in the imperial council.

title: The Precious Gem
summary: A nobleman boasts of an uncut diamond worth a province. Birbal shows the court a gem that shines without fading.

title: The Price of Peace
summary: A neighboring king sends a hostile letter threatening war. Birbal drafts a reply that disarms the enemy without mobilizing a single soldier.

title: Birbal and the Barbers
summary: The barbers of Agra spread wild rumors that send commodity prices soaring. Birbal teaches the guild a humorous lesson in accountability.

title: The Golden Bricks
summary: A nobleman builds a house with bricks covered in gold leaf. Birbal shows him where real golden monuments are built.

title: The Two Brothers
summary: Two farming brothers secretly carry grain sheaves to each other's barn in the night. Birbal presents them to Akbar as the true nobility of the empire.

title: The Wise Minister Test
summary: Akbar asks why Birbal receives higher honors than other ministers. Birbal demonstrates the difference with a single inquiry.

title: The King and the Tiger
summary: A boastful general claims he fears nothing on earth and would fight a tiger bare-handed. Birbal teaches him the difference between courage and madness.

title: The Donkey in Lion's Skin
summary: A foolish courtier dresses in royal silk and tries to terrify the council with fierce commands. Birbal demonstrates why true majesty is quiet.

title: The Fox and the Crow - Birbal version
summary: Birbal retells the famous fable of the crow and the cheese to warn Akbar against a flattering foreign diplomat.

title: Birbal's Mother-in-Law
summary: Birbal's sharp-tongued mother-in-law tests his legendary patience. Birbal handles domestic disputes with the same wit he brings to imperial governance.

title: The Lost Book
summary: A fire destroys the imperial archive, burning a rare treatise on philosophy. Birbal comforts Akbar by demonstrating the permanence of internalized wisdom.

title: The Most Valuable Thing
summary: Akbar asks his ministers to name the most valuable commodity in existence. Birbal names the one treasure that even emperors cannot purchase.

title: The True Worth
summary: A villager finds an uncut diamond and sells it for a loaf of bread. Birbal illustrates the subjective nature of human valuation.

title: Birbal and the Cook
summary: The royal cook serves oversalted soup to the Emperor. Birbal uses an amusing salt test to help the cook correct his recipe without fear.

title: The King and the Elephant
summary: A rogue elephant refuses to move, blocking the palace gates. Birbal moves the giant beast without an iron hook or whip.

title: The Two Thieves
summary: Two burglars rob a merchant's vault, then try to cheat each other out of the loot. Birbal uses their mutual distrust to recover the treasure.

title: The Merchant and the Donkey
summary: Birbal retells the fable of the salt merchant and the lazy donkey to illustrate the danger of habitual deceit.

title: The Rich Man and His Ring
summary: A foolish nobleman searches for a lost ring under a palace lamp instead of in his bedroom. Birbal uses the incident to satirize human escapism.

title: The Clever Thief
summary: A captured thief condemned to the gallows asks for one final boon: to plant a golden pomegranate seed that sprouts only for the innocent.

title: Birbal and the Goldsmith
summary: A dishonest goldsmith replaces pure gold with brass while making an idol. Birbal uses acid and fire to expose the alloy.

title: The Village Idiot
summary: A village boy always chooses a shiny copper coin over a dull silver coin. Akbar thinks the boy is a fool, but Birbal reveals the boy's genius.

title: The King and the Poor Brahmin
summary: Akbar forgets a casual promise of reward made to an impoverished scholar during a hunt. Birbal uses a crooked camel's neck to jog the royal memory.

title: The Talking Tree
summary: Two partners dispute a bag of gold, and one claims a sacred tree spoke from heaven to endorse his claim. Birbal lights a fire to reveal the 'tree's voice.'

title: Birbal and the Snake Charmer
summary: A boastful snake charmer claims his cobras are entirely under his magical control. Birbal shows the court why playing with treachery always ends in ruin.

title: The Price of a Nap
summary: A miserly landlord charges a weary traveler for sleeping in the shadow of his wall. Birbal settles the account with the movement of the sun.

title: The Man Who Counted Breaths
summary: An eccentric ascetic claims he can achieve immortality by counting every breath. Birbal reveals the absurdity of mechanical existence.

title: Birbal and the Fakir
summary: A mendicant asks Akbar for money to build a grand hermitage. Birbal shows the holy man that asking an emperor for gold is merely asking one beggar from another.

title: The Farmer's Son
summary: Akbar challenges a poor farmer's son to solve a riddle that baffled his royal tutors. The boy's practical brilliance wins imperial honor.

title: The Blind Judge
summary: A blind elder in an obscure village settles disputes with uncanny accuracy. Akbar investigates, and Birbal explains the secret of inner sight.

title: The Six Senses
summary: Akbar debates the five physical senses with Birbal. Birbal demonstrates why the sixth sense—common sense—is the supreme captain of life.

title: Birbal and the Carpenter
summary: A hasty carpenter ruins expensive sandalwood timber for the royal throne. Birbal teaches the court a masterclass in precision and foresight.

title: The King and the Pot of Honey
summary: A single dropped spoonful of honey leads to a cascading riot in an ancient fable. Birbal reminds Akbar that small injustices must never be ignored.

title: The Man Who Sold Dreams
summary: A cunning swindler in the Agra market sells golden dreams in clay vials. Birbal uses dream coins to buy out the charlatan's shop.

title: Birbal and the Beggar Woman
summary: An old beggar woman refuses alms thrown into the dust with contempt by a wealthy nobleman. Birbal shows Akbar why respect is greater than charity.

title: The Scholar's True Mother Tongue (HI)
summary: A brilliant visiting polyglot challenges the court of Agra to discover his native language. Birbal uses an unexpected splash of cold water to reveal the truth.

title: Who Dared Pull the Emperor's Mustache? (HI)
summary: Akbar asks his ministers what punishment fits a scoundrel who dared pull his royal mustache. Courtiers demand execution, but Birbal suggests sweetmeats.

title: A Pot Full of Wit (HI)
summary: A neighboring king demands a clay pot filled with pure wit. Birbal fulfills the impossible request using a watermelon vine.

title: The Wax Lion in the Iron Cage (HI)
summary: A foreign emperor sends an iron cage containing a fierce lion without a door or latch. Birbal removes the lion using heat and science.

title: The Man with the Unlucky Face (HI)
summary: Akbar sentences a merchant to death because seeing his face brought bad luck. Birbal shows the Emperor whose face was truly bringing misfortune.

title: The Emperor's Rare Seven-Day Horse (HI)
summary: Akbar challenges Birbal to find a rare horse that is neither black, white, brown, nor grey. Birbal finds the horse with an ingenious calendar condition.

title: The Center of the Earth and the Count of Stars (HI)
summary: A conceited philosopher asks Birbal to identify the center of the earth and the number of hairs on a sheep. Birbal silences him with effortless precision.

title: The Emperor's Milk Reservoir and the Shared Blame (HI)
summary: Akbar tests his citizens' civic honesty by ordering each household to contribute a cup of milk to a dark pool. Morning reveals a reservoir of water.

title: The Blind Men in the City of Agra (HI)
summary: Akbar claims blind men are rare in Agra. Birbal sits on the street mending a shoe and proves that the blind outnumber the sighted ten to one.

title: The Well and the Water Dispute (HI)
summary: A greedy neighbor sells a well to a farmer, then demands rent for the water. Birbal's famous verdict orders the cheat to remove his water immediately.

title: The Two Mothers and the Living Child (HI)
summary: Two women claim the same infant. Birbal orders the baby cut in half, exposing the real mother through her unconditional sacrifice.

title: The Sound of Silver for the Smell of Sweets (HI)
summary: A greedy confectioner demands payment from a beggar who smelled his sweetmeats. Birbal pays the baker with the clinking sound of coins.

title: The Measure of the King's Foot (HI)
summary: A fawning courtier suggests that all land in the empire should be measured using Emperor Akbar's royal foot. Birbal shows the comical chaos of such flattery.

title: The Magic Sticks of the Qazi (HI)
summary: Birbal gives seven suspects identical bamboo sticks, claiming the thief's stick will grow two inches by morning. The thief cuts his stick and confesses.

title: The Five Most Ignorant People in Agra (HI)
summary: Akbar orders Birbal to find the five most foolish men in the empire. Birbal brings three absurd strangers and names the remaining two with brilliant wit.

title: The Emperor's Dream of the Lost Teeth (HI)
summary: An astrologer tells Akbar that all his relatives will die before him, causing royal fury. Birbal interprets the same prophecy with tact, winning praise.

title: The Clever Carpenter's Measure (HI)
summary: A carpenter builds an enormous royal carriage inside a courtyard with a narrow gate. Birbal solves the dilemma without knocking down the palace walls.

title: The Donkey with the Leopard Spots (HI)
summary: A fraudulent trader paints black spots on a donkey and tries to sell it as a rare hunting beast. Birbal unmasks the painted fraud with a bucket of water.

title: The Milk That Turned to Water (HI)
summary: A dishonest dairyman who watered down his milk finds his bag of coins divided by a monkey. Birbal explains the poetic justice of nature.

title: The Test of the True Disciple (HI)
summary: A guru claims his disciples have mastered all desires. Birbal places a plate of fresh mangoes before them in a dark room to test their discipline.

title: The Mirror of Courtly Truth (HI)
summary: Akbar asks why courtiers constantly flatter him, while Birbal speaks blunt truths. Birbal uses a looking glass to illustrate the nature of mirrors.

title: The Secret of the Black Cloth (HI)
summary: Courtiers accuse an honest clerk of treason based on suspicious rumors. Birbal uses a clean white cloth dipped in soot to expose prejudice.

title: The Merchant's Turban and the Camel (HI)
summary: An arrogant merchant wears an impossibly tall turban to impress the court. A passing camel provides an unforgettable lesson in modesty.

title: The Seven Questions of the Persian Ambassador (HI)
summary: A Persian diplomat arrives with seven intricate diplomatic riddles. Birbal answers all seven in a single sentence.

title: The Man Who Stared at the Desert Sun (HI)
summary: An ascetic boasts that his spiritual willpower can overcome the midday sun. Birbal shows the court the difference between faith and stubborn folly.

title: The Two Dervishes at the City Gate (HI)
summary: Two travelers ask about the people of Agra before entering. Birbal gives both opposite answers, revealing a profound psychological truth.

title: The Baker's Uneven Scales (HI)
summary: A baker sues a poor farmer for selling short-weight butter. Birbal uses the baker's own loaf of bread to expose the real thief.

title: The King's Missing Royal Mustache (HI)
summary: Akbar plays a practical joke on his ministers by claiming a hair of his mustache was plucked in the night. Birbal's reaction exposes courtly psychology.

title: The Well That Moved in the Night (HI)
summary: A cunning landlord secretly moves boundary stones to claim a neighbor's stone well. Birbal uses ancient roots and compass measurement to expose the theft.

title: The Greedy Landlord and the Banyan Shade (HI)
summary: A greedy landlord sells the shade of a banyan tree to a weary traveler, then tries to evict him as the sun moves. Birbal resolves the contract.

title: The Price of a Thousand Slaps (HI)
summary: A palace guard demands half the reward of a fisherman presenting an enormous fish to Akbar. Birbal ensures the guard receives his exact half of 'one thousand slaps.'

title: The Emperor's Lightweight Crown (HI)
summary: Akbar complains of a headache from his jewel-encrusted crown. Birbal shows the Emperor that the weight of justice is the real burden of kingship.

title: The Singing Weaver and the Court Poet (HI)
summary: An arrogant court poet mocks an uneducated weaver who sings heavenly hymns at his loom. Birbal demonstrates that true poetry belongs to the heart.

title: The Judge with the Iron Balance (HI)
summary: A provincial judge favors his own relatives in a property dispute. Birbal presents an iron balance that tilts only toward gold.

title: The Camel That Refused to Turn Right (HI)
summary: A stubborn courtier refuses to change his outdated administrative methods. Birbal uses a trained camel to satirize stubborn conservatism.

title: The Oil Merchant and the Silk Seller (HI)
summary: Two merchants dispute ownership of a purse of silver coins. Birbal drops the coins into boiling water to uncover the true owner.

title: The Golden Spoon in the Emperor's Bowl (HI)
summary: Akbar boasts that eating with golden cutlery makes common food taste celestial. Birbal shows the Emperor that true taste resides in hunger.

title: The Three Daughters and the Camels (HI)
summary: A deceased merchant leaves seventeen camels to be divided among three daughters in impossible fractions. Birbal solves the mathematical paradox.

title: The Stolen Mango Grove and the Dry Leaves (HI)
summary: A dishonest landlord claims he purchased an orchard twenty years ago, presenting an aged parchment. Birbal proves the ink is fresh by examining dry leaves.

title: The Parrot with the Broken Wing (HI)
summary: Akbar rescues an injured parrot in the royal gardens and nurses it back to health. Birbal shows the court that kindness is the true measure of kingship.

title: The Brahmin Who Walked on the River (HI)
summary: An ascetic boasts that thirty years of meditation gave him the power to walk across the river Yamuna. Birbal shows him the true market value of his 'miracle.'

title: The Merchant's Mysterious Last Will (HI)
summary: A dying merchant leaves three sealed jars of dirt, bones, and straw to his three sons. Birbal decodes the profound fatherly inheritance.

title: The Emperor's Cracked Mirror (HI)
summary: Akbar smashes a mirror in anger when it distorts his reflection. Birbal uses the broken shards to teach the court a lesson on emotional self-control.

title: The Sentry Who Slept at the Palace Gate (HI)
summary: A young guard falls asleep on duty after nursing his sick mother all night. Birbal saves the soldier from the executioner's sword.

title: The King Who Could Not Sleep (HI)
summary: Akbar suffers from chronic insomnia despite musicians and doctors. Birbal cures the Emperor with a story that has no end.

title: The Clay Pot That Gave Birth to a Cup (HI)
summary: Birbal borrows brass pots from a greedy neighbor and returns them with 'baby' cups. When he later borrows a silver cauldron, he announces it 'died.'

title: The Witness of the Ancient Banyan Tree (HI)
summary: A dishonest traveler denies borrowing money under an old banyan tree. Birbal sends the lender to summon the tree, trapping the borrower in court.

title: The Wise Washerman's Silent Donkey (HI)
summary: A quarrelsome neighbor screams insults at an old washerman. The washerman remains silent, using his donkey to illustrate the beauty of composure.

title: The Flatterer's Grand Feast of Words (HI)
summary: A parasitic courtier promises lavish feasts to guests but never serves food. Birbal invites him to a grand royal dinner of invisible delicacies.

title: The Thief Who Robbed His Own Shadow (HI)
summary: A burglar flees in terror from his own shadow on a moonlit night. Birbal uses the incident to explain how guilt terrifies itself.

title: The Four Seasons in a Single Day (HI)
summary: Akbar asks Birbal whether a mortal can experience Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter in twelve hours. Birbal illustrates the seasons of human emotion.

title: The Emperor's True Portrait (HI)
summary: Akbar is blind in one eye and walks with a limp. Three painters attempt his portrait. Birbal shows how true genius captures reality with grace.

title: The Golden Fishing Net of Agra (HI)
summary: A fisherman rises to become a wealthy minister and keeps a golden net in his palace. Birbal explains the profound memory behind the treasure.

title: The Silver Coin in the Palace Courtyard (HI)
summary: Akbar drops a silver coin on the floor to see which of his noble courtiers will stoop to pick it up. Birbal's reaction provides a lesson in self-respect.

title: The Magic Lamp of Fatehpur Sikri (HI)
summary: A merchant sells an 'Aladdin's lamp' to a gullible prince. Birbal demonstrates that real genies are summoned through human sweat.

title: The Grateful River Fisherman (HI)
summary: A fisherman finds a lost royal emerald in the stomach of a fish and returns it to Akbar. Birbal ensures the honest man's reward blesses his village.

title: The Riddle of the Seven Sealed Pots (HI)
summary: A foreign merchant presents seven identical sealed clay pots containing gold, mud, honey, vinegar, salt, jewels, and ashes. Birbal identifies the contents without opening them.

title: The False Witness and the Clay Dog (HI)
summary: A false witness testifies that he saw a theft committed in pitch-black darkness. Birbal uses a clay dog to shatter the perjurer's testimony.

title: The Man Who Carried His Bullock on His Head (HI)
summary: Birbal meets a traveler carrying his luggage and riding an oxcart, claiming he is sparing the animals. Birbal exposes the comedy of misplaced self-sacrifice.

title: The Barber Who Wanted to Be Prime Minister (HI)
summary: Akbar's royal barber demands to be made Prime Minister for a day. Birbal gives him a complex diplomatic dispute to resolve, curing his delusions.

title: The Peacock's Dance on the Terrace (HI)
summary: A vain prince boasts of his flawless elegance. Birbal uses the peacock's dance to remind him that even the most beautiful creatures have humble feet.

title: The Merchant Who Lost His Memory (HI)
summary: A dishonest merchant claims he forgot borrowing five hundred gold coins due to a medical condition. Birbal restores his 'memory' with an unexpected debt.

title: The Secret of the River Yamuna (HI)
summary: Akbar stands on the riverbank and grieves over the passing of his youth. Birbal uses the flowing current to explain the eternal renewal of existence.

title: The King's Bad Omen at Sunrise (HI)
summary: Akbar encounters an ugly sweeper at sunrise and fears an evil omen. Birbal shows the Emperor that the sweeper is the true benefactor of the city.

title: The Salt Seller and the Cotton Trader (HI)
summary: Two merchants cross a flooded river with salt and cotton. Birbal illustrates the poetic justice of natural elements.

title: The Emperor's Whispering Rose Garden (HI)
summary: Akbar asks why the royal rose garden feels so peaceful compared to the noisy council chamber. Birbal reveals the secret of silent cooperation.

title: The Royal Test of Four Noble Virtues (HI)
summary: Akbar tests four young noble candidates for governorship. Birbal arranges four secret trials to reveal their true character.

title: The Scholar Who Forgot How to Swim (HI)
summary: An arrogant scholar mocks a simple boatman for not studying grammar and astronomy. When the boat leaks, the boatman asks a vital question.

title: The Horse That Grazed on the Palace Roof (HI)
summary: Akbar jokingly commands Birbal to show him a horse grazing on a rooftop. Birbal arranges a spectacle that fulfills the royal whim.

title: The Broken Earthen Water Pot (HI)
summary: A servant weeps uncontrollably after breaking an antique water pot. Birbal uses the broken pieces to teach the court the wisdom of moving forward.

title: The Emperor's Riddle on True Mortality (HI)
summary: Akbar asks what separates an emperor from a beggar after death. Birbal takes the Emperor to an ancient graveyard to find the answer.

title: The Young Cowherd's Sudden Wisdom (HI)
summary: A village boy settles a complex legal dispute between two farmers using a mound of dirt. Akbar and Birbal discover the 'Throne of Vikramaditya.'

title: The Two Beggars at the Golden Gate (HI)
summary: One beggar prays to the Emperor for help, while the other prays to God. Akbar rewards the first beggar, but destiny delivers the gold to the second.

title: The Thief Who Prayed for Heavy Rain (HI)
summary: A thief prays for a torrential downpour so the night watchmen will stay indoors. The resulting flood traps him inside the flooded basement he robbed.

title: The Weaver Who Met a Royal Tiger (HI)
summary: A timid weaver carrying a bolt of bright red cloth encounters a tiger in the jungle. Birbal explains how wit turns terror into survival.

title: The Gold Ring Dropped in the Deep Well (HI)
summary: Akbar drops a diamond ring into a deep, narrow stone crevice where hands cannot reach. Birbal retrieves it using grease and string.

title: The Minister Who Spoke Only in Proverbs (HI)
summary: An obnoxious courtier answers every state crisis by quoting ancient proverbs without taking action. Birbal cures him with an empty proverb feast.

title: The Stolen Silver Anklets of the Dancer (HI)
summary: A pair of musical silver anklets vanishes from a dancer's dressing room. Birbal uses scented oil to catch the culprit among forty palace servants.

title: The Three Ripe Pears of the Orchard (HI)
summary: Akbar asks Birbal how to divide three ripe pears among five hungry royal children without cutting them. Birbal resolves the puzzle with familial love.

title: The Royal Tiger in the Council Hall (HI)
summary: Panic erupts in the palace when a sentry reports a wild tiger loose in the corridors. Birbal investigates and finds an ordinary stray dog and a shadow.

title: The Feast of Invisible Delicacies (HI)
summary: Birbal settles an old score with a stingy noble who invited poor musicians to a 'feast of praises' without serving food.

title: The Royal Physician's Cure for Greed (HI)
summary: A miserly courtier complains of a mysterious ailment that makes him miserable despite wealth. Birbal prescribes the medicine of generosity.

title: The Honest Thief and the Pearl Necklace (HI)
summary: A burglar breaks into a house to steal food for his starving sister, but refuses to take a diamond necklace. Birbal recognizes his noble spark.

title: The Emperor's Silver Beard (HI)
summary: Akbar finds his first grey hair and feels distressed. Birbal turns the moment into a poetic celebration of mature wisdom and leadership.

title: The Clever Tailor's Perfect Measurement (HI)
summary: A tailor sews a coat that fits neither sitting nor standing. Birbal uses the garment to teach the imperial magistrates how laws must adapt to life.

title: The Wandering Dervish and the Bag of Gold (HI)
summary: Akbar tries to bestow a bag of gold upon a wandering dervish who lives under a tree. The dervish's reply reveals the illusion of worldly wealth.

title: The King Who Tried to Sweep the Sand (HI)
summary: Akbar becomes obsessed with clearing a sand dune that continually blows onto the highway. Birbal shows him the folly of fighting nature with brooms.

title: The Merchant's Secret Iron Safe (HI)
summary: A paranoid merchant builds an impenetrable iron vault, only to lock himself inside. Birbal saves the miser and reveals the prison of greed.

title: The Black Sheep and the White Stallion (HI)
summary: A foreign nobleman refuses to walk near dark-skinned peasants, boasting of his fair complexion. Birbal uses black and white animals to dismantle racial vanity.

title: The Arrogant Courtier's Silent Challenge (HI)
summary: A mute mystic challenges Akbar's court using only hand gestures. Birbal decodes the silent philosophical debate with effortless mastery.

title: The Three Travelers and the Loaf of Bread (HI)
summary: Three travelers have only one loaf of bread left. Two scheme to claim the bread through a dream contest, but the third traveler outsmarts them both.

title: The Sage's Secret to Boundless Health (HI)
summary: Akbar asks an ancient centenarian for the secret to a century of vibrant health. Birbal summarizes the rules of living well.

title: The Emperor's Lost Hunting Falcon (HI)
summary: Akbar's prized hunting falcon escapes into a tall tree and refuses to return. Courtiers throw stones in vain, but Birbal coaxes the bird with gentle love.

title: The Farmer Who Sued the Northern Wind (HI)
summary: An unreasonable farmer files a lawsuit against the northern wind for blowing down his dry thatch roof. Birbal delivers a comical verdict that restores sanity.

title: The Potter's Donkey and the Royal War Elephant (HI)
summary: An imperial war elephant mocks an ordinary potter's donkey on a muddy road. When a flash flood strikes, the donkey's agile hoofs save the day.

title: The Magic Water That Reflected Guilt (HI)
summary: A jewel thief hides among thirty palace servants. Birbal uses a bowl of ordinary spring water to make the culprit convict himself.

title: The Scholar with the Mountain of Scrolls (HI)
summary: A pedantic scholar arrives with five cartloads of parchment scrolls, boasting of his unmatched learning. Birbal asks one simple question about life.

title: The Emperor's Final Test of the Nine Jewels (HI)
summary: Akbar tests his famous Nine Jewels (Navratnas) with a final riddle on what preserves an empire. Birbal delivers the crowning answer of the court.
